text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

An all-women panel is weak evidence of almost nothing. Panels of four skew single-sex by chance fairly often, and in risk/compliance functions women are well represented, so the composition is unsurprising. Raising it makes you look aggrieved and undercuts anything substantive you might argue later.

Also, the credential gap may not be a gap. For a *head* of risk modelling, supervisory dialogue — IRB approvals, model validation submissions, stress-test cycles — is frequently the bulk of the role. "Broad regulatory affairs experience" can legitimately outrank a PhD and deeper technical depth.

Your real grievance is the unanswered request. Chase that in writing, cite the deadline in their own recruitment policy, and judge the reasons you get.
